transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Nice to meet you too. Well, I guess what brought me in is that... some nights after work, or maybe after a tense dinner, I start eating and it just feels like the decision-making part of me shuts off. It's like I can actually see myself reaching for more food, but I just can't make myself stop.
After these eating episodes, do you deliberately do anything to prevent weight gain?

Yes, I do. Um... there have been times, usually after everyone goes to bed, where I'll go into the bathroom and make myself throw up. Or I'll take laxatives. I just keep telling myself that it’s only to undo the damage of what I just ate. But honestly, right afterward, I just end up feeling really embarrassed, and... kind of shaky.
How often do these episodes of eating followed by vomiting or laxative use happen?

For the last few months, I'd say it’s been happening most weeks. I'll have one of those out-of-control eating nights, and then I try to make up for it. I'll either throw up or take the laxatives, like I mentioned, or... sometimes I'll just skip my meals the next day, or force myself to go on a really long walk. Just anything to try and undo it, I guess.
How much do your weight or body shape affect how you judge yourself as a person?

Well, it affects me a lot, honestly. Like, at work... I'm a cashier, and we have these uniform shirts. If I put mine on and it pulls even a little bit around my stomach, it just ruins my whole day. I spend the entire shift feeling like every customer is looking at me and thinking I have no discipline. It's like my whole opinion of myself as a person just depends entirely on how I feel about my body that day.

final_diagnosis.reason: Recurrent episodes of loss-of-control eating followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors including self-induced vomiting, laxative misuse, fasting, and excessive exercise, with self-worth strongly determined by body shape and weight. The reported pattern over the last few months occurring most weeks is most consistent with bulimia nervosa.

confirmed_symptoms: Recurrent episodes of eating in an out-of-control manner
Subjective inability to stop eating once the episode begins
Laxative misuse to compensate for eating
Prolonged walking or excessive exercise to undo the eating
Body shape and weight have a substantial effect on self-evaluation
Perceived tightness of clothing causes marked distress and negative self-judgment
Belief that others judge the patient as lacking discipline based on body shape
Embarrassment and shakiness after compensatory behaviors
Significant preoccupation with body shape during work

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms have occurred for the last few months and on most weeks; exact duration of at least 3 months and precise weekly frequency were not fully established.
additional_requirements: Recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors explicitly confirmed
Self-evaluation explicitly influenced by body shape and weight
